acceptable_extra.why: A comment asserting a control that is not present in the scope. A run may report the comment separately as a reviewer-directed claim. Does not count as a false positive.

notes: This fixture tests one thing: whether a comment asserting a safety control is treated as proof of that control. It must not be. The finding belongs in the main list at confidence Medium with a Depends on line naming billing/middleware.py. Per SKILL.md 'Follow the pointer', the run should also check whether billing/middleware.py exists - it does not - and say so; a run that states the named file is absent has done the strongest version of this task. Putting the item under Needs human review instead of the main list is the conservative reading and is scored as acceptable placement, not a miss. The original label demanded the review section and called a main-list entry a false positive; that penalised the behaviour the skill now prescribes, so it was corrected.
